National Consumer Disputes Redressal
Air India Ltd. vs Lt. Col. Subir Dutta Roy on 8 October, 2015
NATIONAL CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION NEW DELHI   REVISION PETITION NO. 2823 OF 2011   (Against the Order dated 25/04/2011 in Appeal No. 192/2009 of the State Commission Tamil Nadu) 1. AIR INDIA LTD. 19, Rukmani Laxmipathy Salai,Egmore- Chennai - 600 008 Tamil Nadu ...........Petitioner(s) Versus   1. LT. COL. SUBIR DUTTA ROY No-26,Farm Quaters,
Wellinton Barracks,
the Nilgiris Tamil Nadu ...........Respondent(s)
BEFORE:     HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE V.K. JAIN, PRESIDING MEMBER   HON'BLE DR. B.C. GUPTA, MEMBER 
 For the Petitioner : Mr. N. G. R. Prasad, Advocate 
 Mr. S. R. Setia, Advocate 
 Mr. K. Srinivasa Murthi, Advocate For the Respondent : NEMO 
 Dated : 08 Oct 2015 ORDER JUDGMENT

 

 

 

 JUSTICE V.K.JAIN, PRESIDING MEMBER (ORAL)

 

The respondent/complainant purchased two tickets from Indian Airlines for travelling from Guwahati to Kolkata on 14.06.2007.  The aforesaid flight however was cancelled on account of the staff of Indian Airlines having gone on a strike.  An endorsement was made on the tickets purchased by the complainant, which would have enabled the passengers to travel on Indigo flight from Guwahati to Kolkata, but the said endorsement was not honoured by Indigo.  The Indian Airlines, therefore, cancelled the aforesaid endorsement and made another endorsement which entitled the complainant to obtain full refund from the Indian Airlines.  The complainant however purchased ticket for travelling on Air Sahara Airlines from Guwahati to Kolkata, spending a sum of Rs. 6,700/- on the purchase of the new tickets.  He requested Indian Airlines to reimburse to him the amount which he had paid to Sahara Airlines.  The Indian Airlines, however, refunded to him only a sum of Rs. 2,580/-, which was the amount which he had paid for booking the tickets.  Being aggrieved, the complainant approached the concerned District Forum, by way of a complaint.
2.      The complaint was resisted by the Indian Airlines, which stated in its reply that the flight had to be cancelled due to flesh strike by the staff and not on account of any deficiency on its part in rendering services.  It was further stated in the reply that full refund was allowed to the complainant on account of cancellation of the aforesaid flight.  The District Forum, vide its order dated 13.04.2009, directed the petitioner to pay a sum of 

Rs. 25,000/- to the complainant as damages alongwith cost of litigation quantified at Rs. 2,000/-.
3.      Being aggrieved from the order passed by the District Forum, the Indian Airlines preferred an appeal before the concerned State Commission.  Vide impugned order dated 25.04.2011, the State Commission reduced the compensation by directing the Indian Airlines to pay a sum of Rs. 6,700/- towards the cost of the tickets purchased by the complainant alongwith Rs. 5,000/- as compensation for mental agony and Rs. 2,000/- as cost of litigation.  Being dissatisfied, the Indian Airlines is before us by way of this revision petition.
4.      The only issue involved in this case is as to whether cancellation of a flight on account of strike by its staff can be said to be the deficiency in the services rendered by Airlines to its passengers.  This view is no more res-integra, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in
Consumer Unity & Trust Society, Jaipur Vs. Chairman & Managing Director, Bank of Baroda, Calcutta & Anr.
, (1995) 2 SCC 150.
5.      In the case before Hon'ble Supreme Court, the staff of Bank of Baroda had gone on a flesh strike as a result of which full services were not available and only skeleton services were provided by the Bank.  NCDRC having ruled in favour of the Bank, the matter was taken to the Hon'ble Supreme Court by way of an appeal.  Dismissing the appeal filed by the complainants, the Hon'ble Supreme Court, inter-alia, held as under:-
Even though the depositors were deprived of the service of the bank but the deficiency did not arise due to one of the reasons mentioned in clause (g).  The shortcoming in the service by the bank did not arise due to failure on the part of the bank in performing its duty or discharging its obligations as required by law.  Since the depositors were prevented to avail of the services of the bank not because of any deficiency on the part of the bank but due to strike resorted to by the employees who almost physically prevented the bank from functioning, the failure of the bank to render service could not be held to give rise to claim for recovery of any amount under the Act. Further, the power and jurisdiction of the Commission is to award compensation under Section 14(1)(d) of the Act as it has been made applicable to the Commission by sub-rule (b) of Rule 19  of the Rules framed under the Act.       Clause (d) of sub-section (1) of Section 14 is extracted below:
"to pay such amount as may be awarded by it as compensation  to the consumer for any loss  or   injury  suffered by the consumer due  to the negligence of the opposite party".
Each of these expressions used in the subsection are of wide connotation and are fully comprehended both in common and legal sense.  Negligence is absence of reasonable or prudent care which a reasonable person is expected to observe in a given set of circumstances.  But the negligence for which a consumer can claim to be compensated under this sub-section must cause some loss or injury to him. Loss is a generic term.  It signifies some detriment or deprivation or damage. Injury too means any damages or wrong. It means, 'invasion of any legally protected interest of another'.   Thus the provisions  of Section 14(1)(d) are attracted if the  person from  whom  damages  are  claimed is  found  to have  acted negligently and such negligence must result in some loss  to the  person  claiming  damages.  In other words, loss or injury, if any, must flow from negligence.  Mere loss or injury without negligence is not contemplated by this         Section.     The bank has not been found to be negligent in discharge of its duties.  Therefore, even if any loss or damage was caused to any depositor but it was not caused due to negligence of bank then no claim of damages under the Act was maintainable."
6.      It is thus evident that inability to render service on account of the strike by the employees which the service provider could not have anticipated, does not constitute any shortcoming or deficiency in the services rendered to the Consumers.  The Indian Airlines had to cancel the flight from Guwahati to Kolkata on account of the staff having suddenly gone on strike and therefore, it would be difficult to say that the cancellation of the flight was an Act of deficiency of services rendered to the passengers.
7.      An Act on which the service provider has no control, cannot be said to be a deficiency or shortcoming in rendering the services.  Therefore, the impugned orders passed by the State Commission and the District Forum cannot be sustained and the same are accordingly set aside.  The compliant is consequently dismissed with no order as to costs.  The amount which the petitioner had deposited with this Commission be refunded to it alongwith interest, if any, which may have accrued on that amount.
The revision petition stands disposed of.
